Because Amitābha Buddha's surpassing light is supremely pure, in this world all the black mountains, snowy mountains, adamantine mountains, and iron-ring mountains, the great and small mountains, rivers and forests, the palaces of gods and humans — every single realm was illumined without exception.]

While these words were being spoken, Amitābha Buddha at once emitted from the palm of his hand immeasurable light, universally illumining all the worlds of the Buddhas. Then all the Buddha-lands appeared before the assembly, as clearly as if one were looking at something an arm's length (one xun) away. Because Amitābha Buddha's surpassing light is supremely pure, in this Sahā world all the black mountains, snowy mountains, adamantine mountains, iron-ring mountains, and the other great and small mountains, rivers and forests, the palaces of gods and humans — every single realm was illumined without exception.

[It is like the rising of the sun, brightly illumining the world. Even the hells, the valleys and streams, and the dark and gloomy places are all thrown wide open, and all are of one color. It is like the water of a kalpa-flood filling the world, in which all things sink and disappear, vast (
huàng
and boundless, and one sees only the great water. That Buddha's light is likewise so.]

It is like the rising of the sun, brightly illumining the world. Even the hells (niraya), the valleys and streams, and the dark and gloomy places are all thrown wide open, and all are of one color. It is like the water of a kalpa-flood (the water of the great flood at the time of the destruction of a kalpa) filling the whole world, in which all things sink and disappear, and one sees only the vast and boundless expanse of great water. Amitābha Buddha's light is likewise so.

(Jieshui) one of the three great calamities, namely the great flood that occurs at the time of the destruction of a kalpa, when water wells up from the water-wheel beneath the earth and rain falls like the axle of a cart and does not stop for many years, so that everything below the Second Dhyāna Heaven is submerged in the great water. (The three great calamities) the calamities of fire, water, and wind that occur when the world is about to be destroyed. (Huangyang (huàng yàng)) describes something vast and boundless. (Haohan) the appearance of water in its abundance.

[All the light of the voice-hearers and bodhisattvas was completely hidden, and only the Buddha's light was seen, bright and resplendent. The four assemblies at this gathering, the eight classes of gods and dragons, humans and non-humans, and the rest all saw the Land of Ultimate Bliss in its manifold adornments.]

All the light of the voice-hearers and bodhisattvas was completely hidden, and only the Buddha's light was seen, bright and resplendent. The four assemblies at this gathering (monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen), the eight classes of gods and dragons, humans and non-humans, and the rest all saw the Land of Ultimate Bliss in its manifold adornments.
(Ren fei ren) another name for the kiṃnara, because the kiṃnara resembles a human yet is not human.

[Amitābha Buddha, upon his lofty seat, majestic in virtue and awe-inspiring, with his marks of beauty and his light, was surrounded by voice-hearers and bodhisattvas who honored him. He was like Mount Sumeru, king of mountains, rising above the surface of the sea, clearly appearing and shining, pure and level. There was no mixture of defilement, nor any beings of different shapes. There was only the adornment of a multitude of treasures, and sages and worthies dwelt together there.]

Amitābha Buddha, upon his lotus jewel seat, majestic in virtue and awe-inspiring, with his marks of beauty and his light, was surrounded and honored by voice-hearers and bodhisattvas. He was like Mount Sumeru, king of mountains, rising above the surface of the sea, clearly appearing and shining, pure and level. There was no mixture of defilement, nor any beings of different shapes. It was entirely the adornment of a multitude of treasures, and sages and worthies dwelt together there.

[Ānanda and all the assembly of bodhisattvas were filled with great joy, leapt up and bowed, touching their heads to the ground, and recited “Namo Amitābha Buddha.” All the gods and people, down to the tiny flying and crawling creatures, who saw this light, had every sickness and suffering at once come to an end, and every worry and affliction at once released. All of them with compassionate minds did good, and were joyful and happy.]

Ānanda and all the assembly of bodhisattvas were filled with great joy, leapt up and bowed, touching their heads to the ground, and recited “Namo Amitābha Buddha.” All the gods and people, down to the tiny flying and crawling creatures, who saw this light, had every sickness and suffering at once come to an end, and every worry and affliction at once released. All of them with compassionate minds did good, and were joyful and happy.

[Bells and chimes, lutes and zithers, and harps — these instruments, without being struck, of themselves all produced the five notes. The gods and people in all the Buddha-lands each took flowers and incense and came into the air, scattering them as offerings.]

Bells and chimes, lutes and zithers, and harps and other instruments, with no one to play them, of themselves all produced the sound of the five notes. The gods and people in all the Buddha-lands each took fresh flowers and precious incense and came into the air, scattering them as offerings.

[At that time the Land of Ultimate Bliss, though it lies beyond a hundred thousand koṭis of Buddha-lands to the west, by the Buddha's majestic power appeared as if face to face, as if with pure divine sight one were looking at a patch of ground an arm's length away. Those in that land saw this land in the same way. They all clearly beheld the Sahā world, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, and the assembly of monks surrounding him as he taught the Dharma.]

At that time, though the Land of Ultimate Bliss lies a hundred thousand koṭis of Buddha-lands away from here, by relying on Amitābha Buddha's majestic power it appeared as if right before the eyes, as if with pure divine sight one were looking at a patch of ground an arm's length (one xun) away. The people of the Land of Ultimate Bliss saw this land in the same way. They all clearly saw the Sahā world, and saw Śākyamuni Buddha surrounded by the assembly of monks as he taught the Dharma.

blocks.text: 39. Birth from a Womb and Transformation Birth

inline.s: (Womb birth and transformation birth) All sentient beings who are reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss are born by transformation in lotus flowers. Among them, those who fall into doubt and regret and are born in the border region within the seven-jeweled city, though they too are born by transformation in a lotus flower, do not have their flower open for five hundred years; they remain within the flower-womb and cannot come forth, and cannot see the Buddha or hear the Dharma, just like a fetus still within its mother's womb. Therefore this is called womb birth. Those born by transformation, however, having been spontaneously transformed within the lotus, emerge in an instant, their bodily marks radiant, their wisdom and merit like those of the bodhisattvas, fully accomplished.
(All are born by transformation in lotus flowers) The Buddha Speaks the Sutra of Immeasurable Pure and Equal Enlightenment (the Han translation) says:

“In the Buddha-lands in the eight directions, above and below, without number, the gods and people and the flying and crawling creatures who are born in the land of Immeasurable Pure Buddha are all born by transformation within the lotus flowers of the seven-jeweled pools.”
The Buddha Speaks the Sutra of Amitābha, the Tathāgata of Threefold Enlightenment, Sagara-Buddha, the Buddha-Treasury, Crossing Over the Human Realm (the Wu translation) says:

“The second vow: when I attain Buddhahood, let there be no women in my land. Should women wish to come and be born in my land, they shall at once become men. All the countless gods and people, and the flying and crawling creatures, who come to be born in my land, shall all be born by transformation within the lotus flowers of the seven-jeweled pools.”

[At that time the Buddha told Ānanda and Bodhisattva Maitreya: Do you see the Land of Ultimate Bliss — its palaces and pavilions, its springs, pools, forests, and trees — fully possessed of subtle, pure, and adorned beauty or not
(anciently the same as “or not”)
? Do you see the gods of the desire realm, up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, raining down fragrant flowers throughout the Buddha-land or not? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have seen it.]

At that time the World-Honored One asked Ānanda and Bodhisattva Maitreya: Do you see that the Land of Ultimate Bliss — its palaces and pavilions, its springs, pools, forests, and trees — is fully possessed of subtle, pure, and adorned beauty? Do you see the gods of the desire realm, up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, raining down fragrant flowers throughout the Buddha-land? Ānanda replied: Yes, I have seen it.
[Have you heard Amitābha Buddha's great voice proclaimed throughout all worlds, teaching sentient beings or not? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have heard it.]
The World-Honored One asked again: Have you heard Amitābha Buddha's great voice proclaimed throughout all worlds, teaching sentient beings or not? Ānanda replied: Yes, I have heard it.

[The Buddha said: Do you see the host of pure practitioners in that land, roaming and dwelling in the air with palaces following them, without any obstruction, going everywhere in the ten directions to make offerings to all the Buddhas or not? And do you see them reciting the Buddha's name without interruption? And do you see all the many birds dwelling in the air, uttering all kinds of sounds, all of them transformed creations — do you see them all? Maitreya said: As the Buddha has said, I see each and every one.]

The World-Honored One asked again: Do you see the host of pure practitioners in that land (the Land of Ultimate Bliss), roaming and dwelling (traveling and residing) in the air with palaces following them, going everywhere in the ten directions without any obstruction to make offerings to all the Buddhas or not? And do you see them reciting the Buddha's name without interruption (reciting the Buddha's name without interruption by deluded thoughts) or not? And do you see all the many birds dwelling in the air, uttering all kinds of sounds, all of them transformed creations — do you all see them? Bodhisattva Maitreya said: As the Buddha has said, I see each and every one.
Hua zuo) produced by the Buddha’s spiritual power, and not living beings.

[The Buddha told Maitreya: Among the people of that land there are some born from a womb — do you see them too? Maitreya said: World-Honored One, I see those in the Land of Ultimate Bliss who dwell in the flower-womb, like the Yāma gods dwelling in their palaces. And I see other beings, within the lotus flower, seated cross-legged (
jiā fū
, spontaneously transformed, emerging in an instant. For what reason do the people of that land include some born from a womb and some born by transformation?]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: Do you also see that among the people of the Land of Ultimate Bliss there are some born from a womb? Bodhisattva Maitreya said: World-Honored One, I see those in the Land of Ultimate Bliss who dwell in the flower-womb, as if dwelling in palaces in the Yāma Heaven. And I also see other beings seated cross-legged within the lotus flower, spontaneously transformed, emerging in an instant. For what cause and condition do the people of that land (the Land of Ultimate Bliss) include some born from a womb and some born by transformation?
(Jiafu (
jiā fū
) zuo)

Placing both feet crossed upon the left and right thighs is called the “full cross-legged posture.” Placing only the left foot over the right thigh, or only the right foot over the left thigh, is called the “half cross-legged posture.”
Shunxi er chu
] The Sutra of the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Life (the Tang translation) says:

“Should there be sentient beings who cut off doubt and regret, accumulate roots of goodness, seek the Buddha-wisdom and even the vast wisdom, and have faith in their own roots of goodness, such a person, seated cross-legged within the lotus flower, is suddenly transformed, emerging in an instant.”

blocks.text: 40. The Borderland and the City of Doubt

inline.s: [The Buddha told Maitreya: Should there be sentient beings who cultivate all merits with a mind of doubt and wish to be born in that land, yet do not understand the Buddha-wisdom, the inconceivable wisdom, the inexpressible wisdom, the vast wisdom of the Mahāyāna, and the unequaled, incomparable, supreme and foremost wisdom — toward these wisdoms they harbor doubt and do not believe. Yet they still believe in offense and blessing, cultivate the roots of goodness, and wish to be born in that land.]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: Should there be sentient beings who cultivate all merits with a mind of doubt and wish to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, yet are unable to believe in and understand the Buddha-wisdom, the inconceivable wisdom, the inexpressible wisdom, the vast wisdom of the Mahāyāna, and the unequaled, incomparable, supreme and foremost wisdom, and who harbor doubt and do not believe in these holy wisdoms — yet still believe in the karmic retribution of offense and blessing, cultivate the roots of goodness, and wish to be born in that land.

[There are also sentient beings who accumulate roots of goodness, seeking the Buddha-wisdom, the universal wisdom, the unequaled wisdom, and the majestic, vast, and inconceivable wisdom. Yet in their own roots of goodness they cannot give rise to faith.]

There are also sentient beings who accumulate roots of goodness, seeking the Buddha-wisdom, the universal wisdom, the unequaled wisdom, and the majestic, vast, and inconceivable wisdom. Yet in their own roots of goodness they are unable to give rise to faith.

[Therefore, when those people are about to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, their will wavers and they have nothing to rely on firmly. Yet they still recite without cease, and binding up their good vows as the root, they too attain rebirth.]

When the two kinds of people described above — those who do not believe in the Buddha-wisdom and those who do not believe in their own roots of goodness — are about to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, their will wavers and they have nothing to rely on firmly. Yet they still recite the Buddha's name without cease, and binding up their good vows as the root, they too attain rebirth.

[These people, by this cause and condition, though born in that land, cannot go forward to where Immeasurable Life dwells, but stop at the border of the Buddha-land, in a seven-jeweled city. The Buddha does not make it so; it is their own bodily conduct and the direction of their own minds. There are also jeweled pools and lotus flowers, and within them they spontaneously receive a body. Their food and drink and their happiness are like those of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.]
These people

by such causes and conditions, though born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, cannot go forward to where the Buddha dwells, but stop within the seven-jeweled city at the border of the Buddha-land. It is not that Amitābha Buddha causes them to be born there (in the borderland city of doubt); rather, it is their own bodily conduct and what their own minds turn toward, and so they are spontaneously born there. There too there are jeweled pools and lotus flowers, and within the lotus they spontaneously receive a body. Their food and drink and their happiness are like those of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
(The Buddha does not make it so; it is their own bodily conduct and the direction of their own minds) The Avataṃsaka Sutra says:
“One should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm: all is made by mind alone.”

Because “when the mind arises, all dharmas arise,” hell, heaven, the Pure Land, and Buddha-lands are all manifested by one's own mind. Where the body tends is entirely drawn along by one's own thoughts, and therefore it is said that “the mind turns toward it of itself.” (Spontaneously receiving a body) hence it is not a birth from a mother's womb in this world.

[But they remain in the flower-womb and cannot come forth. For five hundred years they cannot see the Buddha, cannot hear the sutras and Dharma, and cannot see the bodhisattvas, voice-hearers, and holy assembly. These people's wisdom is unclear, and their knowledge of the sutras is scant; their minds do not open and understand, and their hearts are not joyful. Therefore, in that land they are called womb-born.]

But they remain in the flower-womb and cannot come out. For five hundred years they cannot see the Buddha, cannot hear the sutras and Dharma, and cannot see the bodhisattvas, voice-hearers, and holy assembly. These people's wisdom is unclear, and their knowledge of the sutras is scant; their minds do not open and understand, and their hearts are not joyful. This is what is called womb birth.

[Should there be sentient beings who clearly believe in the Buddha-wisdom, and even in the supreme wisdom, who cut off doubt, have faith in their own roots of goodness, perform all merits, and with utmost sincerity dedicate them — they all, within the lotus flowers of the seven-jeweled pools, seated cross-legged, are spontaneously transformed, emerging in an instant, their bodily marks radiant, their wisdom and merit like those of the bodhisattvas, fully accomplished.]

Should there be sentient beings who firmly believe in the Buddha-wisdom, and even in the supreme wisdom, who cut off doubt, and who also believe in their own roots of goodness, perform all merits, and with utmost sincerity dedicate them — they all, within the jeweled pools of that Buddha's land, in the lotus flowers, are spontaneously transformed and seated cross-legged in an instant. In a moment, their bodily marks are radiant and their wisdom and merit are like those of the bodhisattvas, fully accomplished.

[Maitreya, you should know that those born by transformation have surpassing wisdom. Those born from a womb, for five hundred years, do not see the Three Jewels, do not know the bodhisattvas' methods of practice, cannot cultivate merit, and have no means to serve Amitābha Buddha. You should know that these people, in former lives, had no wisdom, and this was brought about by doubt.]

Maitreya, you should know that those born by transformation are so because their wisdom surpasses that of the womb-born. As for those born from a womb, for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels (they do not see Amitābha Buddha, do not hear the sutras and Dharma, and do not see the bodhisattvas, voice-hearers, and holy assembly), do not know the bodhisattvas' methods of practice, cannot cultivate merit, and have no means to serve Amitābha Buddha. You should know that these people, in a former life (the life before their rebirth), had no wisdom, and this was brought about by doubt.

blocks.text: 41. When Delusion Is Exhausted, One Sees the Buddha

inline.s: [Suppose a wheel-turning sage king had a prison of seven jewels, and a prince committed an offense and was confined within it. Its storied towers and splendid
(qǐ)

halls, jeweled canopies and golden beds, railings, windows, couches, and seats were all adorned with rare and wondrous treasures. His food, drink, and clothing were like those of the wheel-turning king, yet his two feet were bound with golden chains. Would the young princes take delight in this?]

Suppose a wheel-turning sage king had a prison of seven jewels, and a prince committed an offense and was confined within it. There too were storied towers and splendid halls, jeweled canopies and golden beds, railings, windows, couches, and seats, all adorned with rare and wondrous treasures. His food, drink, and clothing were like those of the wheel-turning king, yet his two feet were bound with golden chains. Would the young princes confined in that prison take delight in such a life?
(Qi (qǐ) dian) splendid palaces.

[Maitreya said: No, World-Honored One. While he is imprisoned, his mind is not at ease, and he seeks release by every kind of means. He begs the close ministers, but his wish is never granted. Only when the wheel-turning king is pleased does he obtain release.]

Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: No, World-Honored One! When they are imprisoned, their minds are not at ease, and they seek release by every kind of means. They beg the close ministers, but their wish is never granted. Only when the wheel-turning king is pleased do they obtain release.
(You zhi (zhí)) imprisonment. (Jin chen) the ministers close to the ruler's side.

[The Buddha told Maitreya: These sentient beings are likewise so. Should any fall into doubt and regret, unable to give rise to faith in the Buddha's wisdoms or in their own roots of goodness, yet because they hear the Buddha's name and give rise to faith, though they are born in that land, they cannot emerge from within the lotus flower.]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: The womb-born sentient beings are likewise so. If they are unable to believe in the Buddha-wisdom or in their own roots of goodness, yet because they hear the Buddha's name and give rise to faith, though they are born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, they remain within the lotus womb of the borderland city of doubt and cannot come out.

[In that place the flower-womb seems like a garden or a palace. Why is that? Because within it all is pure, without any defilement or evil. Yet for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels, cannot make offerings to and serve the Buddhas, and are far removed from all surpassing roots of goodness. They take this as suffering and give rise to no delight.]

Dwelling within the lotus womb of the borderland city of doubt, they also feel it to be like a garden or a palace. Why? Because within it all is pure, without any defilement or evil. Yet for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels (they do not see Amitābha Buddha, do not hear the sutras and Dharma, and do not see the bodhisattvas, voice-hearers, and holy assembly), cannot make offerings to and serve the Buddhas, and are far removed from all surpassing roots of goodness. They take this as suffering and give rise to no delight.

[If these sentient beings recognize the root of their offense and deeply repent and reproach themselves, seeking to leave that place, then when the faults of their past lives have been fully exhausted, they thereafter emerge. They at once go to where Immeasurable Life dwells and hear the sutras and Dharma. In time they too will open and understand and be joyful, and will also be able to make offerings everywhere to countless and immeasurable Buddhas and cultivate all merits.]

If these sentient beings recognize where the root of their offense lies, they deeply repent and correct themselves, seeking to leave the borderland city of doubt. When the faults of doubt from their past lives have been fully repented and purified, they can then emerge from the lotus womb. They at once go to where Amitābha Buddha dwells and hear the sutras and Dharma. In time they too will open and understand and be joyful, and will also be able to make offerings everywhere to countless and immeasurable Buddhas and cultivate all merits.

[Maitreya, you should know that doubt is a great harm to the bodhisattvas and a loss of great benefit. Therefore you should clearly believe in the Buddha's unsurpassed wisdom and in your own roots of goodness.]

Maitreya, you should know that doubt is a great harm to the bodhisattvas and a loss of great benefit. Therefore you should firmly believe in the Buddha's unsurpassed wisdom and in your own roots of goodness.

[Maitreya said: Why is it that a certain class of sentient beings in this world, though they too cultivate good, do not seek rebirth? The Buddha told Maitreya: These sentient beings have shallow and slight wisdom. Discriminating, they judge the West to be inferior to the heavens, and therefore take no delight in it and do not seek to be born there. Maitreya said: These sentient beings make false and deluded discriminations. If they do not seek the Buddha-land, how shall they escape the round of rebirth?]

Bodhisattva Maitreya said: Why is it that in this world there is still a class of sentient beings who, though they too cultivate good, do not seek birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha told Maitreya: These sentient beings have shallow and slight wisdom. Discriminating, they judge the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss to be without the heavenly realms' pleasures of desire, and therefore they take no delight in it and do not seek birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Bodhisattva Maitreya said: These sentient beings make false and mistaken discriminations. If they do not seek birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, how can they escape the round of rebirth?

(If they do not seek the Buddha-land, how shall they escape the round of rebirth?) If they do not seek birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, how can they escape the round of rebirth? Though gods and humans have the pleasures of desire, once their blessing is exhausted and their life ends, they continue to turn on the wheel within the six paths.

[The Buddha said: The roots of goodness these people have planted cannot be free of marks; they do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, but cling deeply to worldly pleasures and human blessings. Though they cultivate blessing, they seek the fruit of gods and humans. When they obtain their reward, they have every abundance, yet they cannot escape the prison of the three realms. Even should their parents, wives, and children, their kin and relations, wish to save and deliver them, the king of wrong views and karma is not yet forsaken, and they remain forever within the round of rebirth, never at ease.]

The Buddha said: The roots of goodness these sentient beings have planted cannot be free of marks; they do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, but cling deeply to worldly pleasures and human blessings. Though they too cultivate blessing, they seek the fruit of humans and gods. When they obtain their reward, they have every abundance, yet they cannot escape the prison of the three realms, and when their blessing is exhausted they fall again, with endless later misfortune. After their life ends, even should their parents, wives, and children, their kin and relations, recite the sutras and cultivate the Dharma, wishing to save and deliver them, their king of wrong views and karma is not yet forsaken and they do not give rise to right faith, and so they remain forever within the round of rebirth, never at ease.
(The king of wrong views and karma) Because

of wrong views they do not give rise to right faith, and therefore wrong view is in truth the king of all evil karma. Hence it is said, “the king of wrong views and karma.” (When blessing is exhausted they fall again, with endless later misfortune) This is what is commonly called the “grievance of three lives.” (The grievance of three lives) Because one cultivates in this life, in the next life one enjoys the reward of blessing, and thereupon relying on that blessing one commits evil, which brings about one's fall in the life after that (the third life). Even when the karma of hell has been dissolved, one is then reborn again as a hungry ghost or an animal, and to regain a human body is harder still! Therefore the World-Honored One asked Ānanda, holding soil in his hand: “Is there more soil in my hand, or more soil in the great earth?” Ānanda replied: “There is more soil in the great earth.” The Buddha said: “Those who gain a human body are like the soil in my hand; those who lose a human body are like the soil of the great earth.” Hence, “through ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lives, not one person is there to rely on”! Therefore, if a practitioner does not put an end to birth and death in this life, then after three lives suffering and evil retribution are endless, and so it is called the “grievance of three lives.” (See
The Grievance of Three Lives

[You see the deluded and foolish, who plant no roots of goodness, but with worldly cleverness and glib argument merely increase their wrong minds. How shall they escape the great calamity of birth and death? There are also sentient beings who, though they plant roots of goodness and create a great field of blessing, grasp at marks and discriminate, with deep and heavy attachment of feeling. Seeking to escape the round of rebirth, they in the end cannot attain it.]

You see those deluded and foolish people, who plant no roots of goodness, but with worldly cleverness and glib argument merely increase their wrong minds. How can they escape the great calamity of birth and death? There are also sentient beings who, though they plant roots of goodness and create a great field of blessing, grasp at marks and discriminate, with deep and heavy attachment of feeling. Seeking in this way to escape the round of rebirth, they in the end cannot attain it.
(Worldly cleverness and glib argument)
Worldly cleverness is the petty cleverness of ordinary people in the world, and glib argument is using that petty cleverness to argue over right and wrong.

[If with the wisdom of no marks one plants the roots of every virtue, and one's body and mind are pure, far removed from discrimination, seeking birth in the pure land and tending toward the Buddha's bodhi, one shall be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and forever attain liberation.]

If with the wisdom of no marks one plants the roots of every virtue, and one's body and mind are pure, far removed from discrimination, seeking birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and tending toward the Buddha's bodhi, one shall certainly be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and forever attain liberation.

[Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: In this Sahā world and in all the Buddha-lands, how many are the non-regressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha told Maitreya: In this world there are seven hundred and twenty koṭis of bodhisattvas who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue, and who shall be born in that land. As for the bodhisattvas of lesser practice who cultivate merit and shall be reborn there, their number cannot be reckoned.]

Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: In this Sahā world, and in all the Buddha-lands, how many are the non-regressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: In this Sahā world there are seven hundred and twenty koṭis of non-regressing bodhisattvas who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue, and who shall be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. As for the bodhisattvas of lesser practice who cultivate merit and shall be reborn there, their number cannot be reckoned.

(The Sahā world) The word “Sahā” originally referred to the southern continent of Jambudvīpa where we dwell, and in later ages it came to mean the three-thousand-great-thousand world taught and transformed by Śākyamuni Buddha, so that the whole of the hundred koṭis of Sumeru-worlds is collectively called Sahā, with Śākyamuni honored as the original teacher of the Sahā world. “The Sahā world” in this passage refers to the three-thousand-great-thousand world taught and transformed by Śākyamuni Buddha. (Bodhisattvas of lesser practice) bodhisattvas who have not yet reached the stage of non-regression.

[Not only do the bodhisattvas of my land go to be born in that land; it is likewise so in the Buddha-lands of other directions. From the Buddha-land of Far-Shining Radiance, a hundred and eighty koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are born in that land. In the northeast, from the Buddha-land of Precious Treasury, ninety koṭis of non-regressing bodhisattvas shall be born in that land. From the Buddha-lands of Immeasurable Sound, of Light, of Dragons and Gods, of Surpassing Power, of the Lion, of Freedom from Dust, of Virtue's Foremost, of the Benevolent King, and of Flowered Banners, those non-regressing bodhisattvas who shall be reborn there number either tens of koṭis, or hundreds of thousands of koṭis, or even ten thousand koṭis.]

Not only do the bodhisattvas of my Buddha-land go to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; it is likewise so in the Buddha-lands of other directions. From the Buddha-land of Far-Shining Radiance, a hundred and eighty koṭis of great bodhisattvas are born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the northeast, from the Buddha-land of Precious Treasury, ninety koṭis of non-regressing bodhisattvas shall be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. From the Buddha-lands of Immeasurable Sound, of Light, of Dragons and Gods, of Surpassing Power, of the Lion, of Freedom from Dust, of Virtue's Foremost, of the Benevolent King, and of Flowered Banners, those non-regressing bodhisattvas who shall be reborn there number either tens of koṭis, or hundreds of thousands of koṭis, or even ten thousand koṭis.
The above is a brief account of the names of eleven Buddha-lands of other directions and the numbers of bodhisattvas born there.

[The twelfth Buddha is named Supreme Flower. He has countless multitudes of bodhisattvas, all of them non-regressing. In wisdom and courage they are mighty, and they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas. Endowed with great diligence, they set their resolve upon the One Vehicle. Within seven days they can gather in the firm dharmas cultivated by great beings through a hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas. All such bodhisattvas shall be reborn there.]

The twelfth Buddha is named Supreme Flower. He has countless multitudes of bodhisattvas, all of them at the stage of non-regression. In wisdom and courage they are mighty, and they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas. Endowed with great diligence, they vow and set their resolve upon the One Vehicle (final Buddhahood). Within seven days they can gather in the firm dharmas cultivated by great beings through a hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas. All such bodhisattvas shall be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Firm dharmas) the dharma of non-regression.

[The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearless. He has seven hundred and ninety koṭis of great bodhisattvas, and lesser bodhisattvas and monks beyond all reckoning, all of whom shall be reborn there. Were one to speak only the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions and of the multitudes of bodhisattvas who shall be reborn there, a kalpa would not suffice to exhaust them.]

The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearless. He has seventy-nine billion great bodhisattvas, as well as incalculable lesser bodhisattvas and monks, all of whom will be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. As for the names of the Buddhas of the worlds of the ten directions and the hosts of bodhisattvas who will be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, if one were to speak only their names, a whole kalpa would not suffice to tell them all.

The Buddha told Maitreya: Observe those bodhisattvas and mahāsattvas, who have well obtained benefit. If there are good men and good women who hear the name of Amitabha Buddha and are able to give rise to a single thought of joyful delight, who take refuge, revere and worship, and
practice in accordance with the teaching

. Know that such a person will obtain great benefit and will gain the merits spoken of above. His mind is neither base nor arrogant; the good roots he accomplishes all increase and advance. Know that such a person is not of the Lesser Vehicle; in my Dharma he is named a foremost disciple.

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: Look at those great bodhisattvas who are reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss — they have well obtained benefit. If there are good men and good women who hear the name of Amitabha Buddha and are able to give rise to a single thought of joyful delight, who take refuge, revere and worship, and practice in accordance with the teaching, then know that such a person obtains great benefit and will gain the merits spoken of above. His mind is neither base nor arrogant and conceited; the good roots he accomplishes all increase and advance. Know that such a person is not of the Lesser Vehicle; in my Dharma he is named a foremost disciple.

Well obtained benefit: One of the highest grade of the highest class sees the Buddha and hears the Dharma, immediately awakens to non-arising, and ascends to the eighth ground. Therefore it is said, well obtained benefit.
The Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life says:

When that person is about to be born in that land, because of his diligent and courageous effort, Amitabha Tathāgata, together with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, countless manifest Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of monks, the great assembly of śrāvakas, immeasurable gods, and seven-jeweled palaces — with Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara bearing a diamond platform and Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta — comes before the practitioner. Amitabha Buddha sends forth a great light that illumines the practitioner's body and, together with all the bodhisattvas, extends his hands in welcome. Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and countless bodhisattvas praise the practitioner and urge his mind onward. Seeing this, the practitioner is filled with joy and leaps up; he sees his own body riding upon the diamond platform, following behind the Buddha, and in the space of a finger-snap is born in that land. Having been born in that land, he sees the Buddha's physical body complete in all its marks and sees all the bodhisattvas complete in their physical forms, while radiant bejeweled forests proclaim the wondrous Dharma. Having heard it,
he immediately awakens to the patience of the non-arising of dharmas

, and in the space of a moment he journeys throughout the ten directions to serve all the Buddhas, and before each Buddha receives a prophecy in turn. Returning to his own land, he obtains immeasurable hundreds of thousands of dhāraṇī-gates. This is what is meant by one of the highest grade of the highest class.

The Eighth Ground: The eighth of the ten grounds of the bodhisattva, called the Ground of Immovability. On this ground the bodhisattva abides in the patience of non-arising, cuts off all deliberate exertion, and his body and mind are still and extinguished, like empty space; he accomplishes the pāramitā of vow and, with the mind of nirvāṇa, is serene and unmoving — hence it is called the Ground of Immovability. The Ten Grounds: Among the fifty-two stages of the bodhisattva's practice, the fifth set of ten is called the Ten Grounds. On these ten grounds one gradually opens the Buddha-realm and accomplishes all-knowing wisdom; since this already belongs to the stage of the sages, it is also called the Ten Sages.

Therefore I say to you, gods, humans, and asuras of the world: you should rejoice in and cultivate this Dharma and give rise to a heart of rare resolve. In this sutra, look upon it as your teacher and guide. Those who wish to bring countless sentient beings to swiftly and securely abide without falling back, and who wish to behold that vast and majestic, marvelously adorned Buddha-land, pure in its reception and replete with merit, should upraise vigorous effort and listen to this Dharma-gate.

Therefore, I tell you all — gods, humans, and asuras — you should rejoice in and cultivate the Pure Land Dharma-gate, giving rise to a heart of rare resolve. In this sutra, look upon it as your teacher and guide. Those who wish to bring countless sentient beings to swiftly and securely abide without falling back, and who wish to behold that vast and majestic, marvelously adorned Buddha-land, pure in its reception and replete with merit, should upraise vigorous effort and listen to and receive this Pure Land Dharma-gate.
To look upon it as one's teacher in this sutra: Through what this sutra teaches, one is able to give rise to genuine faith and to practice accordingly.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a heart of regression, flattery, or deceit. Even were you to enter a great fire, you should not doubt or regret. Why is that? Because those countless millions of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate, listening to it with reverence and never turning against it. Many are the bodhisattvas who wished to hear this sutra but could not. Therefore, you should seek this Dharma.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a heart of regression, flattery, or deceit. Even were you to enter a great fire, you should not doubt or regret. Why? Because those countless millions of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle and wondrous Pure Land Dharma-gate, listening to it with reverence and never turning against it. Many are the bodhisattvas who wished to hear this sutra but could not. Therefore, you should ardently seek this Pure Land Dharma-gate.

In the future, even down to the time when the True Dharma is extinguished, there will be sentient beings who have planted roots of virtue and, in past ages, made offerings to countless Buddhas. Through the added power of those Tathāgatas' majestic might, they are able to gain this vast Dharma-gate and to receive and uphold it, and shall attain the vast all-knowing wisdom. In that Dharma they shall gain vast and profound understanding and experience great joy. They shall widely proclaim it to others and always delight in its practice.

In the future, even down to the time when the True Dharma is extinguished, there will be sentient beings who have planted roots of virtue and, in past lives, made offerings to countless Buddhas. Because they receive the awesome spiritual power and added protection of Amitabha Buddha, they are able to gain this vast Dharma-gate (the Pure Land Dharma-gate), to receive and uphold it, and shall attain the vast all-knowing wisdom. In that Dharma (the Pure Land Dharma-gate) they shall gain vast and profound understanding and experience great joy. They shall proclaim it widely to others and always delight in its practice.

The vast Dharma-gate: In the age of the Final Dharma, even though a hundred million people cultivate, hardly one attains the Way; only by relying on recitation of the Buddha's name can one cross the sea of birth and death. Therefore, the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the Dharma-gate that broadly delivers sentient beings, and for that reason it is called the great expansive Dharma-gate. All-knowing wisdom: the wisdom within all wisdoms; that is, the Buddha's wisdom.

All good men and good women who are able to seek this Dharma — whether they have sought it in the past, are now seeking it, or shall seek it in the future — will all obtain beneficial fruits. You should abide in it without doubt, plant roots of virtue, and constantly cultivate, so that you are free of doubt and obstruction and never enter the prison-house fashioned of every kind of precious treasure.

All good men and good women who are able to seek this Dharma (the Pure Land Dharma-gate) — whether they have sought it, are now seeking it, or shall seek it — will all obtain beneficial fruits. You should abide in it without doubt, plant roots of virtue, and constantly cultivate, so that you are free of doubt and obstruction and never enter the prison-house of every kind of wealth and worldly attainment.

Maitreya, beings of great majesty and virtue such as these are able to give rise to faith in the vast and extraordinary gate of the Buddha-Dharma. Because this Dharma is not heard by some, a hundred million bodhisattvas have fallen back from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Maitreya, beings of great majesty and virtue such as these — those who seek this Dharma, whether already, now, or in the future — are able to give rise to faith in the vast, extraordinary, and skillful-means Dharma-gate of the Buddha-Dharma. Because this Dharma-gate (the vast and extraordinary gate) is not heard by them, a hundred million bodhisattvas have fallen back from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

The vast and extraordinary gate: a vast and uniquely skillful-means Dharma-gate, that is, the Dharma-gate of chanting the Buddha's name. The uniquely skillful-means Dharma-gate: chanting the Buddha's name is the most expedient of all expedients and the shortest of all short-cuts, and is therefore called a uniquely skillful-means Dharma-gate. The most expedient of expedients, the shortest of short-cuts: the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the most expedient and the most direct of all Dharma-gates, and chanting the Buddha's name is again the most expedient and most direct within the Pure Land Dharma-gate. The ancient masters praised it as the short-cut beyond all short-cuts.

The vast and extraordinary gate: vast means that the Dharma-gate of chanting the Buddha's name reaches beings of all three faculties, gathering in both the sharp and the dull; it is the great Dharma by which the Tathāgata universally delivers all beings, sage above and ordinary below, so that in this very life they may put an end to birth and death and swiftly realize Buddhahood.

If any sentient beings copy this sutra, make offerings to it, uphold and recite it; if for even a moment they expound it to others and encourage them to listen; if they give rise to no worry or affliction but day and night contemplate that land and the Buddha's merits — they shall never fall back from the unsurpassed Way.

If any sentient beings copy this sutra, make offerings to it, uphold and recite it; if for even a moment they expound it to others and encourage them to listen; if they give rise to no worry or affliction but day and night contemplate the Western Land of Utmost Bliss and the merits of Amitabha Buddha — they shall never fall back from the unsurpassed Way (the Way of Buddhahood).

At the moment of their death, even if the entire three-thousand-great-thousand world were filled with a great fire, such a person could transcend it and be reborn in that land. This person has already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi. All Tathāgatas together praise them. Therefore you should single-mindedly believe and accept this sutra and uphold, recite, proclaim, and practice it.

At the moment of their death, even if the entire three-thousand-great-thousand world were filled with a great fire, they could transcend it and be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. These persons have already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi (the prophecy that they will certainly become Buddhas in the future). All Tathāgatas together praise them. Therefore, you should single-mindedly believe and accept this sutra and uphold, recite, proclaim, and practice it (practice in accordance with its teachings).

Now I have spoken this sutra and its Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, so that they may see Amitabha Buddha and all that is in his land. Whatever should be done, they may all seek it. Do not, after my passing, give rise to doubt again.

Now I have spoken this sutra and its Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, so that they may see Amitabha Buddha and all that is in his land. Whatever should be done — namely, the faith, the vow, and the practice for seeking rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss — you should strive to accomplish. Do not, after my passing, give rise to doubt again.

In the ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be entirely extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially leave this sutra to remain for a hundred years. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all be able to gain deliverance.

In the ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be entirely extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially leave this sutra to abide for a hundred years more. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all be able to gain deliverance.
The extinction of the scriptures and the Way: The Jingying Commentary says:

As for the extinction of the scriptures and the Way in the ages to come, this sets forth the matter of the Dharma being extinguished in the future. Śākyamuni's True Dharma lasts five hundred years, the Semblance Dharma a thousand years, and the Final Dharma ten thousand years. When all these have passed, it is called complete extinction.
Master Shandao's Verses of Praise in Repentance and Rebirth says:
When the Three Jewels are extinguished after ten thousand years, this sutra alone remains for a hundred years.

True Dharma, Semblance Dharma, and Final Dharma: The Buddha-Dharma is divided into three periods — the period of the True Dharma, the period of the Semblance Dharma, and the period of the Final Dharma. In the period of the True Dharma, although the Buddha has passed away, the Dharma and its practice have not changed; there is teaching, there is practice, and there are those who realize the fruit — this is called the period of the True Dharma. In the period of the Semblance Dharma, semblance means similarity; it resembles the True Dharma but is not the True Dharma. In this period there is teaching and there is practice, but those who realize the fruit are already very few. In the period of the Final Dharma, final means feeble; this period turns to feebleness, and there is only teaching without practice and, all the more, none who realize the fruit.

A Tathāgata's appearance in the world is hard to encounter and hard to see. The sutras and the Way of all Buddhas are hard to gain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend, hear the Dharma, and be able to practice it — this, too, is hard. If one hears this sutra and joyfully believes and upholds it, this is the hardest of all hardships; nothing surpasses this hardship.

A Tathāgata's arising in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The sutras and the Way of all Buddhas are hard to gain and hard to hear. To encounter a good spiritual friend, hear the Buddha-Dharma, and immediately put it into practice (to practice as it teaches) — this, too, is hard. If one hears this sutra and joyfully believes and upholds it, this is the hardest of hardships; nothing surpasses it.

If any sentient being, upon hearing the Buddha's name, has a pure and compassionate heart, leaps up with joy, has the hair of his body stand on end, or sheds tears — all this is because in former lives he has cultivated the Buddha-Way, and so he is no ordinary person.

If any sentient being, upon hearing the name of Amitabha Buddha, has a pure and compassionate heart, leaps with joy, has the hair of his body stand on end, or sheds tears — all this is because in former lives he has cultivated the Buddha-Way, and therefore he is no ordinary person.
To hear the Buddha's name: that is, to hear the name of Amitabha Buddha.
The Sutra of Immeasurable Life as spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation) renders it as
having heard the name of that Buddha,
the Assembly of the Tathāgata Amitāyus (the Tang translation) renders it as
hearing the name of that Buddha,
the Sutra of Mahāyāna Immeasurable Life and its Adornment (the Song translation) renders it as
having heard the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life,
respectively.

If, upon hearing the Buddha's name, one's mind is full of doubt and mistrust, and one has no faith whatever in the words of the Buddha's scriptures — such a one has come from the evil paths; his past calamities are not yet exhausted and he is not yet destined for deliverance. For this reason his mind is full of doubt, and he does not believe and take refuge.

If, upon hearing the name of Amitabha Buddha, one's mind is full of doubt and mistrust, and one has no faith whatever in the words of the Buddha's scriptures — such a one has come from the evil paths; his past calamities are not yet exhausted and he is not yet due for deliverance. Therefore his mind is full of doubt, and he cannot believe and accept.
Faith and taking refuge: to trust and to turn toward the Buddha.

The Buddha told Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathāgatas — the deep Dharma of the ten powers and the fearlessnesses, unobstructed and unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is not easily encountered. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to proclaim. Even times of firm and deep faith are hard to meet.

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathāgatas — the deep Dharma of the ten powers and the fearlessnesses, unobstructed and unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is very hard to encounter. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to proclaim. Those of firm and deep faith are rarely to be found.

Now I proclaim this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, as is fitting, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you to guard it greatly, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let sentient beings tumble into the six realms and suffer every kind of peril and pain.

Now I proclaim, as is fitting, this vast and subtle Pure Land Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you to guard it greatly, in order to benefit all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let them tumble into the six realms and suffer every kind of peril and pain.
Entrusting to you:

Bodhisattva Maitreya is a bodhisattva with but one life remaining, who presently dwells in the Inner Court of the Tuṣita Heaven. After four thousand years (namely, five billion six hundred seventy million years in human reckoning), he will descend to be born in the human world and realize Buddhahood beneath the dragon-flower tree in the Hua-lin Grove; following after Śākyamuni Buddha, he is the fifth Tathāgata of the Bhadra Kalpa.
The Buddha told Maitreya:

Now I proclaim this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, as is fitting, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you to guard it greatly, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night.
This shows that, after Bodhisattva Maitreya realizes Buddhahood in this Sahā world, he too will proclaim and spread this Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
The long night: a simile for the long darkness of ignorance through which ordinary beings, from beginningless kalpas, transmigrate in birth and death.

You should diligently cultivate, in accord with my teachings. Be filial to the Buddha and always remember the grace of your teacher. Let this Dharma abide long and never be extinguished. Uphold it steadfastly — do not destroy or lose it. Do not act wilfully, adding to or subtracting from the sutra and the Dharma.

You should diligently and earnestly cultivate, in accord with my teachings. Be filial to the Buddha and always remember the grace of your original teacher. Let this Dharma abide long and never be extinguished. Uphold it steadfastly — do not destroy or lose it. Do not act wilfully, adding to or subtracting from the sutra and the Dharma.

If one constantly recollects without interruption, one swiftly attains the Way. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. What the Tathāgata practices, you also should follow. Plant and cultivate merit and virtue, and seek rebirth in the Land of Utmost Bliss.

Those who constantly recollect the name of Amitabha Buddha, continuous and unbroken, swiftly attain the Way. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. What the Tathāgata practices, you should likewise follow. Plant and cultivate merit and virtue, and seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
Constant recollection without end: constant recollection means always recollecting the name of Amitabha Buddha; without end means that thought after thought continues without break.

blocks.text: 47. First Hearing Through Merit and Wisdom

inline.s: Then the Blessed One pronounced these verses:
At that time the World-Honored One spoke this gāthā:
Had one not cultivated merit and wisdom in the past,
one could not have heard this True Dharma
(that is, not having heard the Pure Land Dharma-gate, or though hearing it, being unable to give rise to faith and take it in);
but one who has already made offerings to the Tathāgatas will joyfully believe in this.
Those who are evil, proud, slothful, and of wrong views can hardly trust the Tathāgata's subtle Dharma; like a blind man dwelling always in the dark, they cannot lead another onto the road.
Only those who have planted all good roots before the Buddha can cultivate this world-saving practice
(the Pure Land Dharma-gate);
having heard it, they uphold it and transcribe it, recite it, praise it, proclaim it, and make offerings to it.
The world-saving practice: The Pure Land Dharma-gate is able to broadly deliver sentient beings and lead them out of birth and death; hence it is called the world-saving practice.

Thus with a single mind one seeks the Pure Land and is certain to be reborn in the Land of Utmost Bliss; even if a great fire filled the whole three-thousand world, relying on the Buddha's majestic power all would transcend it.

The Tathāgata's deep and vast sea of wisdom only a Buddha and a Buddha can know; though śrāvakas ponder the Buddha's wisdom for a myriad kalpas and exhaust all their psychic powers, they cannot fathom it.
The Tathāgata's merits only a Buddha knows; only the World-Honored One can reveal them. Human life is hard to obtain and a Buddha is hard to meet
(hard to encounter),
and to hear the Dharma with faith and wisdom is the hardest of all hardships.

If sentient beings are to become Buddhas, their practice must transcend that of Samantabhadra and reach the further shore; therefore, all of you who are learned and wise should believe in my teaching — these words of truth.

This wondrous Dharma — how fortunate to have heard it! You should always recollect the Buddha and give rise to joy. Uphold it and broadly deliver those in the stream of birth and death; the Buddha declares such a person a true good friend.

Uphold it to broadly deliver those in the stream of birth and death: to uphold this sutra and, by means of this Pure Land Dharma-gate, to broadly deliver sentient beings drowned in birth and death. Of the stream refers to persons or things of the same kind. The stream of birth and death is the flood of birth and death, that is, sentient beings submerged in birth and death. The Buddha declares such a person a true good friend: the Buddha says this person is truly a good friend (a spiritual guide) of sentient beings.

Then, when the Blessed One had spoken this sutra and its Dharma, in the human and heavenly worlds twelve thousand koṭi-koṭi of sentient beings were freed from dust and defilement and attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭi of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred monks, with all their defilements entirely exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭi of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merits of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭi of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭi and a hundred thousand sentient beings, who had never set their minds upon the unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time set their minds upon it. They planted roots of virtue and, wishing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitabha Buddha, they will all be reborn in that Tathāgata's land. In various other regions, one after another, they will realize Buddhahood, all bearing the same name — the Tathāgata Wonderful Sound.
At that time, when the Blessed One had finished speaking this sutra and its Dharma, in the human and heavenly worlds twelve thousand koṭi-koṭi of sentient beings were freed from dust and defilement
(affliction),

and attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭi of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred monks, with their defilements exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭi of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merits of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭi of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭi and a hundred thousand sentient beings, who had never set their minds upon the unsurpassed bodhi, now set their minds upon it for the first time. Planting roots of virtue and wishing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitabha Buddha, they will all be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. In each of the ten directions, one after another, they will realize Buddhahood, all bearing the same name — the Tathāgata Wonderful Sound.

The pure Dharma-eye: to see the true truth clearly is called the pure Dharma-eye. All defilements exhausted: the afflictions are entirely ended, and one attains the fruit of Arhatship. The patience of non-retrogression: one abides in the principle of non-retrogression with a thought that never wavers.

Furthermore, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, both those now reborn and those who will be reborn in the future who see Amitabha Buddha number eight koṭi-koṭi each; they receive the prophecy, attain the Dharma-patience, and realize unsurpassed bodhi. All these sentient beings, through the karmic conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, all attain rebirth in the Land of Utmost Bliss.

Moreover, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, those who are now reborn and those who will be reborn in the future who see Amitabha Buddha number eight koṭi-koṭi each; they receive the prophecy, attain the Dharma-patience, and accomplish unsurpassed bodhi (perfectly realizing the Buddha-fruit). All these sentient beings, through the karmic conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, all attain rebirth in the Land of Utmost Bliss.

The Dharma-patience: the three kinds of patience in the forty-eighth vow — the first, second, and third Dharma-patience (the patience of echo and sound, the patience of gentle compliance, and the patience of the non-arising of Dharmas).

Then the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and there appeared all manner of rare and miraculous transformations; it emitted a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Moreover, the gods in the sky made wonderful music and uttered voices of rejoicing. Even the gods of the form-realm all heard it and exclaimed that nothing like it had ever been. Immeasurable wonderful flowers came raining down in profusion.

At that time the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and there appeared all manner of rare and miraculous transformations; it emitted a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Moreover, gods and men in the sky played wonderful music and sounded voices of rejoicing. Even the gods of the form-realm all heard it and marveled that such a thing had never been. Immeasurable wonderful flowers came falling down in profusion.

The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas — devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, the whole great assembly — hearing what the Buddha had said, all experienced great joy, believed and accepted it, and practiced it.

The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas — the devas, nāgas, and eight classes of beings, the entire great assembly — having heard what the Buddha taught, all rejoiced greatly, believed and accepted it, and practiced it.
